p: Behold, with all the holy Ushpizin
we find that they made a feast and a meal
at the time that their aspect was clarified in its completeness.
on the day of the weaning," etc. (Bereishis 21:8).
וַיִּזְבַּח יַעֲקֹב זֶבַח בָּהָר (שָׁם לא, נד),
"And Yaakov offered a sacrifice on the mountain" (ibid. 31:54) —
all as we discussed on the previous days.
And with Yosef as well we find,
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה צב, ד)
and our Sages of blessed memory said (Bereishis Rabbah 92:4)
that it was a Shabbos meal.
But with Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
we do not find that he made a meal,
removed from the matters of this world,
devoted only to Torah from Heaven.
And with Aharon HaKohen we find,
"And Aharon came to eat bread," etc.,
for this was his entire matter,
"the bread of his God he shall eat."
Only with Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
do we not find that he made a feast and a meal;
that all his days he was steeped in fasting,
as is brought in the Midrash
(יַלְקוּט שִׁמְעוֹנִי דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א, רֶמֶז תתר״פ)
עַל פָּסוּק (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כב, יד)
"And behold, in my affliction I have prepared,"
he consecrated the cost of the meal
"and my heart is slain within me,"
that he slew it through fasting.
The explanation is that all the six middos
and have illumination of their own,
whereas the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
corresponds to the aspect of Malchus,
which has nothing of its own,
only what the middos bestow upon it.
It is like the holiness of the day of Shabbos
relative to the six days of the week,
for the blessings of all of them are in it.
on all the days of Sukkos
we perform the shakings with the lulav
to draw down the inner light,
and we also make a circuit with the lulav
in order to draw down the surrounding light —
according to that day's own aspect;
except that on the seventh day
in order to draw from all the surrounding lights
And each day we say one Hoshana
according to that day's own aspect:
as there are detailed in this Hoshana
all the descriptions and praises of Hashem Yisbarach.
corresponds to the aspect of Yitzchak,
of the place of the Mikdash,
as our Sages of blessed memory said (Zevachim 62a)
that they built the Mizbeach in the place
where they recognized the ashes of Yitzchak;
וְכֵן נֶאֱמַר אַחַר הָעֲקֵידָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית כב, יד)
and so it says after the Akeidah (Bereishis 22:14),
on the mountain of Hashem it shall be seen."
which speaks of the holiness of the Jewish nation,
from whom the holiness of Israel descended.
הוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
corresponds to the aspect of Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
כִּי הָיָה בָּרוּר זֹאת לְנֶגֶד עֵינָיו
for this was clear before his eyes,
that there is no savior besides Him, may He be blessed.
corresponds to the aspect of Aharon HaKohen,
שׁוֹשְׁבִינָא דְּמַטְרוֹנִיתָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג כ, א),
the groomsman of the Matronisa (Zohar III 20a);
that in all the lowly things on earth
there is found the resting of His holiness, may He be blessed.
And Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
is the groomsman of the King (ibid.),
meaning that the root of holiness
is in the highest of heights,
removed from all the matters of this world,
הוּא בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
is the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
who has nothing of his own,
but rather depends on the merit of others —
And although there is also mentioned there
"for the sake of the merit of Dovid,"
הוּא רַק מִצַּד בְּחִינַת כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
that is only from the aspect of Knesses Yisrael,
for his soul is comprised of them.
regarding Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
that it says of him (Shmuel II 12:20),
"He asked, and they set bread before him, and he ate."
after he had received his punishment through the child,
which they were afraid to tell him,
"Behold, while the child was alive," etc.
But according to his aspect precisely,
it was then that he made a meal,
when it became known to him
that his punishment had been exacted in this world;
that is, "one is obligated to bless," etc.,
"just as one blesses on the good" —
the completion of the clarification came precisely
at the time he was afflicted in this world;
as our Sages of blessed memory said (Berachos 7b)
about "A psalm of Dovid, when he fled," etc.
that he said, "Why is the strap hanging?
For he was the first soul
that was sunk into the kelipah
through the flaw of Adam HaRishon,
he refined his soul through self-affliction,
"a time when man ruled over man
to his own hurt" — precisely so.
We have already spoken of this:
that the number of the mikra'ei kodesh
is seven days in the year,
הַיְינוּ יוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וּשְׁבִיעִי שֶׁל פֶּסַח,
namely the first and seventh days of Pesach,
וְיוֹם רִאשׁוֹן וְיוֹם הַשְּׁמִינִי שֶׁל חַג,
and the first day and the eighth day of the Chag;
and the seventh day is Yom Kippur.
It is like the holiness of the day of Shabbos
relative to the six days of the week:
is the Shabbos of the mikra'ei kodesh,
וְהוּא נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
And it corresponds to the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him;
לָכֵן גַּם כֵּן אֵין בּוֹ אֲכִילָה וּשְׁתִיָּה,
therefore it too has no eating and drinking,
כִּי כֵן הוּא בְּחִינַת מִדָּה הַשְּׁבִיעִי
for such is the aspect of the seventh middah
from the side of the holiness of Israel:
from all the pleasures of this world.
However, with Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him,
מָצִינוּ בּוֹ דַּיְיקָא (מְלָכִים א ג, טו)
"and he made a feast for all his servants,"
וְאָמְרוּ זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה א, א, ט)
and our Sages of blessed memory said (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:1:9)
that one makes a feast upon completing the Torah.
through the holiness of the meal,
כִּי כְּמוֹ שֶׁהָיָה מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּנוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
For just as Moshe Rabbeinu, peace be upon him,
the root of the Written Torah,
הָיָה מְסוּלָּק מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
was removed from all the matters of this world,
while the aspect of Aharon HaKohen was precisely
to draw the aspect of holiness
into all the physical matters of this world,
וּכְמוֹ כֵן בְּחִינַת דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
so too the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהוּא שׁוֹרֶשׁ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
who is the root of Torah she'b'al peh,
הָיָה מְסוּלָּק מִכָּל עִנְיְנֵי הָעוֹלָם הַזֶּה,
was removed from all the matters of this world,
וּכְנֶגֶד זֶה הָיָה שְׁלֹמֹה בְּנוֹ דַּיְיקָא
and correspondingly his son Shlomo was the one precisely
to draw holiness into all physical things
and into the pleasures of this world.
The aspects of Dovid and Shlomo
הֵמָּה נֶגֶד בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף
correspond to the aspects of Mashiach ben Yosef
as it was said to Dovid
(דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כב, ח; כח, ג)
"Only you shall not build the House,
for you are a man of wars,
and you have shed much blood."
This is the aspect of Mashiach ben Yosef,
with the nations of the world;
and this is the trait of Yosef HaTzaddik:
אֵיזֶהוּ גִבּוֹר הַכּוֹבֵשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ (אָבוֹת ד, א).
"Who is mighty? One who conquers his inclination" (Avos 4:1).
For the leaven in the dough
and the subjugation by the kingdoms are one matter:
just as there is found in the heart
the surge of the yetzer hara,
the nations of the world in actuality,
who have this power in the kelipah,
who rise up against a person,
and one must do battle with them.
לָכֵן הָיָה לְדָוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
Therefore Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him, had
until he subdued them under his hand
בְּעֵת שֶׁכָּבַשׁ אֶת יִצְרוֹ מִכֹּל וָכֹל.
at the time when he conquered his inclination entirely.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן הוּא עִנְיַן מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן יוֹסֵף,
So too is the matter of Mashiach ben Yosef,
from the aspect of "the mighty one who conquers his inclination."
that the aspect of Yosef is
the war against the inclination before the sin,
so as not to be enticed by its counsel;
while the aspect of Dovid HaMelech, peace be upon him,
is the war even after the downfall
so that his heart not fall because of it,
as is known, that he is "the man who was raised up,"
עוּלָּהּ שֶׁל תְּשׁוּבָה (עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ה, א).
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah (Avodah Zarah 5a).
אָמְנָם בְּחִינַת שְׁלֹמֹה הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
But the aspect of Shlomo HaMelech, peace be upon him —
הוּא נִקְרָא אִישׁ מְנוּחָה (דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים א כב, ט),
he is called "a man of rest" (Divrei HaYamim I 22:9),
for he has no war at all
from the side of the yetzer hara,
since it is already subdued beneath him;
no war at all with the nations of the world.
וְזֶה יִהְיֶה בְּחִינַת מָשִׁיחַ בֶּן דָּוִד,
And this will be the aspect of Mashiach ben Dovid,
"And all kings shall bow down to him," etc.,
because there will be ultimate completion
also in the nullification of the provocation of the yetzer hara,
"And I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh."
